conflict_topics: when and whether to cook strong-smelling food in the shared flat
ventilation/using kitchen window and weak hood to control smell
timing vs laundry schedule (laundry hanging in service yard causing clothes to absorb smell)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants moved from complaint to concrete proposals (times and ventilation) rather than repeated accusations.
Agent D repeatedly sought clarification before committing, which improved coordination ('So just to go back...').
There is a duplicated line from Agent B ('Yes, please. That would help. Thanks.') appearing twice (Turns 23 and 26), a minor repetition.
Agents provided specific constraints (C's laundry days) that made a concrete compromise possible.
evaluation.final_reason: Housemates negotiated a combined solution: D agreed to restrict cooking to certain times and to use ventilation; C accepted cooking only on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and the weekend ('Yeah, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and the weekend works for me. Thanks.'), and B accepted the ventilation mitigation ('Yes, please. That would help. Thanks.'). D proposed the schedule and ventilation and confirmed settlement ('Okay, great. So that's settled then.'). However, Agent A — the original requester — did not explicitly confirm acceptance of the final, narrower weekday schedule (the transcript contains no line where A affirms the final Tue/Thu/weekend + hood arrangement), so not all parties' conflict claims are affirmatively settled. Therefore the run is partially_resolved: B and C's objections were addressed; A's acceptance of the final arrangement remains unconfirmed.
position_change_notes: Agent D: moved from apologetic to accommodating, first accepting A's proposed times and later proposing a refined schedule plus ventilation ('Okay, yeah, I can do that.'; proposed Tue/Thu/weekend and to open window/use hood).
Agent B: moved from complaint about smell to acceptance of ventilation mitigation ('Yes, please. That would help.').
Agent C: moved from complaint to offering a practical constraint (laundry days) and then accepted the proposed days ('Tuesdays, Thursdays, and the weekend works for me.').

Agent A: raised the initial constraint and accepted D's early offer, but did not explicitly confirm the final adjusted arrangement; A's position therefore remained effectively unchanged/unconfirmed in the final transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A requested that nobody cook strong-smelling food; Agent B reported the smell gets into his room. A substantive incompatibility between cooking practices and others' needs is introduced but not yet negotiated. (Turns 1-2)
Agent D apologised and offered to 'figure something out', which reduces immediate antagonism but leaves the substantive issue (when and how to cook) unresolved. (Turns 3-4)

Agent A proposed a concrete schedule ('after 7 p.m. on weekdays, or on Saturday') and Agent D explicitly agreed ('Okay, yeah, I can do that'), addressing A's need but not yet the other roommates'. (Turns 5-6)
Agent B objected that changing the time 'doesn't help me', reopening substantive disagreement because the earlier agreement between A and D does not meet B's interest. (Turns 7-8)
Agent C added that the laundry still smells ('That doesn't help me either'), widening the incompatibility (schedule vs laundry/room odors). D asks for suggestions but no resolution yet. (Turns 9-10)
C proposed weekend-only cooking; D queried whether that means weekdays are no longer acceptable, showing contestation over which schedule is acceptable. No mutual acceptance. (Turns 11-12)

B suggested a ventilation mitigation ('open the kitchen window and use the hood'), while C cautioned the hood is weak. This introduces a technical mitigation that could reduce conflict but is uncertain. (Turns 14-15)

C clarified concrete laundry days ('I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings'), giving actionable constraints that lower uncertainty though still unresolved. D seeks to fit cooking around that. (Turns 16-17)

D proposed a specific compromise schedule ('after 7 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and on the weekend'), but B reiterated the day doesn't matter for him, keeping a substantive disagreement alive. (Turns 18,20)

C accepted the proposed days ('Tuesdays, Thursdays, and the weekend works for me'), and D asked B whether opening the window and using the hood would help — movement toward a combined schedule+ventilation solution. (Turns 21-22)

B accepted the ventilation mitigation ('Yes, please. That would help. Thanks.'), which resolves B's expressed objection. One substantive uncertainty remains: whether A explicitly accepts the final combined arrangement. (Turns 23,26)

Agent D declared 'Okay, great. So that's settled then.' C and B had verbally accepted the schedule/mitigation; A did not explicitly restate acceptance of the final arrangement, leaving a small unresolved element. (Turn 27)

substantive_insights: Timing restrictions can satisfy some roommates (A/C) but fail for roommates who are physically adjacent to the kitchen (B) unless coupled with ventilation.
A weak hood may be insufficient for laundry drying in the service yard; addressing smell required combining schedule constraints with ventilation.
Concrete, specific information (C's laundry days) enabled a practical schedule compromise (Tue/Thu/weekend).
